answer: Each year the divers swim the reef transects and count the coral heads, filing the count under the transect's own number. A lantern count copied from another reef fails the survey: at the voyage of the transect the coral must match the reef the divers actually swam, and a copied count names coral from another sea. Forging a survey takes a dive team, a boat and 11,300 in wages and fuel, while the ocean record in the reef office is kept for thirty years, so a transect whose coral was never counted is dropped from the chart.
